title: The Sanctions Illusion
gist: Jamal Ibrahim Haidar and Seyed Mohammad Karimi argue that the defense of sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran rests on a false premise — that they are a 'scalpel' pressuring elites while sparing citizens — when in reality they inflict widespread civilian suffering that rarely produces political change.

insights.claim: Governments portray economic sanctions as a precision instrument — 'a scalpel rather than a sword' — capable of pressuring ruling elites while sparing ordinary citizens, but that central premise is untrue.
insights.speaker: JAMAL IBRAHIM HAIDAR
insights.so_what: Challenges the policy assumption underpinning sanctions regimes — if their premise is false, expect growing debate over their legitimacy and durability, a variable for sanctioned-asset and commodity exposure.
insights.quote: they portray them as a precision instrument—a scalpel rather than a sword—capable of pressuring ruling elites while sparing ordinary citizens

insights.claim: Sweeping financial sanctions inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, but this rarely translates into the political change their proponents intend.
insights.speaker: JAMAL IBRAHIM HAIDAR
insights.so_what: If sanctions predictably fail to force regime change, the tail risk is prolonged stalemate rather than resolution — relevant to how long sanctioned economies and their commodity flows stay constrained.
insights.quote: while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change

insights.claim: US President Donald Trump is imposing an 'economic D-Day' on Iran, described as one of the most sweeping acts of economic coercion in modern history.
insights.speaker: JAMAL IBRAHIM HAIDAR
insights.so_what: Escalation of maximum-pressure sanctions on Iran keeps a geopolitical risk premium on oil and Middle East assets, with the authors implying limited odds of the intended political payoff.
insights.quote: like the “economic D-Day” US President Donald Trump is now imposing on Iran
